newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israeli shares close higher in thin trading.
newsitem.headline: Israeli shares close higher in thin trading.

text.p: Tel Aviv shares closed higher on Wednesday in thin trading as investors remained sidelined, traders said.
The benchmark Mishtanim index of the top 100 shares rose 0.81 percent, or 1.55 points, to 194.05 on a low all-share turnover of 51 million shekels against 48 million on Tuesday.
The Maof 25 blue chip index gained 0.72 percent to 203.75.
"Volume continues to be very low and most of the activity is concentrated in very few Maof shares," said Uri Schur at Eyal Securities.
"The earning reports published today were within expectations and the market didn't show too much interest in them," Schur said.
"The market continues to show weakness with many shares moving on low volume," said a trader at Bank Leumi.

Teva Pharmaceutical Industries, the most active share, rose 1.75 percent to 148,800 on volume of 3.6 million shekels. Lehman Brothers raised its 1996 full-year earnings forecast for the company to $1.41 per American depositary receipt (ADR) from $1.38.
Teva also announced on Wednesday it had won approval from Israel's Health Ministry to market its multiple sclerosis treatment Copaxone. Israel is the first country to approve sale of the new drug.
Elron Electronic Industries closed unchanged at 11,297 after it reported third-quarter per share earnings of $0.12, unchanged from the year-earlier period.
American Israeli Paper Mills gained 0.25 percent to 12,477 despite reporting a decline in third-quarter net profit to 8.6 million shekels from 16 million shekels a year earlier.
Other active shares included Bank Leumi, which rose 1.0 percent 380 on turnover of 2.8 million shekels, and Bank Hapoalim, which closed unchanged at 454 on volume of 2.7 million shekels.
